title: Postgram
summary: A prototype for digital postcards tied to a place. Recipients have to visit that location before they can open the photo and message.
problem: We wanted to test a digital interaction that depended on a physical experience. In Postgram, location controls access to the message, so the whole journey is designed around proximity.
audience: People who want to leave a photo and message somewhere for a friend to discover in that place.
role: Product and engineering in a three-person team with AuroraJobs' former CTO and Product Owner.
responsibilities: Full flow to create a postcard: photo, message and location.
Proximity unlock: the recipient only sees the content when they're on the spot.
Onboarding that explains the mechanic without fuss.
decisions: Make location the condition for seeing the message rather than an extra piece of metadata.
Keep the journey short around an unusual condition: being physically present.
Rails to ship the full cycle without inventing extra infrastructure.
outcomes: A working prototype with the create, receive and open cycle.
A complete mechanic linking creation, location, proximity, and opening.
contribution: Product and engineering work that turned a location constraint into a complete journey.
proof: Working prototype covering postcard creation and opening.
